source_refs.title: Cetacean Navigators
source_refs.relevance: Primary authority for corridor government, berth allocation, courts, hazard records, wet/dry station life, multimodal route boards, low-resource access failures, revenue, and the fixture-marked Brineglass hearing-room elaboration.

source_refs.title: Lightsail Express
source_refs.relevance: Grounds a carrier whose value and political leverage come from dependable bulk movement, corridor reputation, and delivery of food, data, and refugees.

source_refs.title: Ganymede Route Compact
source_refs.relevance: Grounds the recognized legal position of Navigator councils in convoy arbitration, shared hazard ledgers, rescue obligations, and route-steward representation.

source_refs.title: Uplift
source_refs.relevance: Grounds uplift as nonhuman biological lineages with cognition and institutional access shaped by interfaces, habitat scaffolds, labor history, and contested recognition.

source_refs.title: Territories
source_refs.relevance: Grounds territory as route, dock, life-support, record, and maintenance custody; Ganymede as route-law junction; and outer-system authority through waystations, rescue capacity, and long supply intervals.

source_refs.title: Identity Abyss

source_refs.title: Narrative Themes
source_refs.relevance: Grounds usable evidence, institutional plurality, material care, disability access, records, rescue capacity, and the risk that maintenance or accommodation authority exports costs to the person who needs it.

source_refs.title: Pirate Metagame Novella Cast Bible
source_refs.relevance: A 2671 continuity example establishes a bottlenose uplifted Navigator as a Corridor Court and Rescue Ledger witness. This fixture uses only the lineage and institutional compatibility, not the named character or that story's plot.

historical_context.location: Brineglass Waystation, a small low-resource stop in the Cetacean Navigator outer-corridor network; the fixture does not assign it a more precise canonical orbit.
historical_context.summary: A routine local berth hearing tests a Lightsail Express hazard-diversion claim. The shared route board loses the pressure-pulse channel at the decisive interval, forcing the wet-side clerk to choose how accessibility, evidence custody, docking time, cargo movement, and claimant testimony share the cost.

public_facts.text: Navigator Waystation Councils allocate berths and local maintenance while Corridor Courts arbitrate broken convoy commitments and related claims.
Navigator route authority rests on common records, rescue obligations, certification, convoy guarantees, arbitration, and reciprocal dependency rather than continuous territorial ownership.
Brineglass's hearing room shares one record across wet and dry circulation using light, sound, pressure pulse, and raised notation, with evidence slates transferred through a sealed drawer.
A clerk may pause the berth clock for manual translation, but the delay consumes docking time and records the requesting party.
Lightsail Express depends on corridor reputation and reliable delivery across routes where trust is scarce.

ambient_pressures.text: Low-resource station improvisation makes access failures ordinary and politically consequential rather than exceptional malice.
A rescue diversion can protect lives while imposing fuel, schedule, bond, berth, and cargo costs that still need an accountable record.
Recognition and access are infrastructural: a formal right to participate is thin when the required interface or translation is unavailable at the decision point.

groups.label: Brineglass Waystation hearing staff and local council
institutional_logic: Keep a low-resource wet/dry station usable by making berth, rescue, maintenance, and evidence decisions other corridor participants will accept.
material_incentives: Turn scarce docking minutes, translation labor, and working interface channels into defensible local decisions.
internal_virtues: Decisions that travel with their evidence
internal_shames: A hearing completed only because one participant could not access it
Losing a berth window to avoidable maintenance
Pretending a diagnostic is a repair
prestige_markers: A difficult hearing that remains legible to wet and dry participants
A pause with a clear owner and reason
A record accepted at the next station
taboo_triggers: Treating one body-specific interface as optional decoration
Claiming rich-hub standards while billing poor-station delays to users
emotional_display_norms: Frustration is compressed into dry procedure, small jokes, and exact correction rather than theatrical outrage.
trust_defaults: Trust synchronized records and visible provenance first; trust expertise when its boundary is marked; distrust urgency that asks evidence to become simpler.
speech_register_cues: Short decisions tied to material effects

groups.label: Lightsail Express carrier crew
institutional_logic: Remain the dependable carrier by making rescue, delay, and deviation legible inside route and bond records.
material_incentives: Preserve berth access, bond standing, delivery schedules, and the credibility required for future convoy work.
internal_virtues: Rescue that does not abandon the rest of the convoy
internal_shames: A late ship without an admissible reason
A rescue story that looks like careless routing
Cargo waiting while procedure repeats itself
prestige_markers: A bond that survives a real diversion
A crew and cargo delivered through a disputed corridor
A hazard record accepted beyond the originating port
taboo_triggers: Being treated as unreliable after spending resources on rescue
A station exporting its equipment failure into the carrier's record
emotional_display_norms: Fear and anger appear as schedule arithmetic, compressed summaries, and controlled challenges to the record.
trust_defaults: Trust route institutions because other carriers do, while contesting any local process that threatens the reputation those institutions certify.
speech_register_cues: Rare direct appeals to the lives behind the ledger

groups.label: Uplifted Navigator participants
institutional_logic: Turn trained route cognition, shared records, habitat interfaces, and irreplaceable coordination into political authority answerable to other corridor participants.
material_incentives: Maintain wet-side access, recognized testimony, route work, and the infrastructure that makes participation more than a legal promise.
internal_virtues: Expertise whose evidence can be challenged
internal_shames: Letting embodied skill be used as an excuse for inaccessible records
Allowing dependence to harden into unanswerable authority
prestige_markers: Rescue records that change route standing
A hearing conducted through shared interfaces
taboo_triggers: Dryside access treated as the default form of reality
emotional_display_norms: Body orientation, timing, low clicks, movement through water, and concise translated speech carry as much social meaning as human facial expression.
trust_defaults: Trust demonstrated competence and common records; remain alert to carriers, ports, and courts that value Navigator cognition while externalizing its habitat and access costs.
speech_register_cues: Visible pauses before claims that exceed the evidence

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: A low-resource station can provide a real accommodation while still making the requester publicly own the delay and its docking cost.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Prompt staff and claimants to argue through clocks, requester fields, translation labor, and cargo consequences instead of abstract inclusion speeches.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: A carrier can do the humane thing during transit and still need to prove the deviation was operationally justified to keep future work.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Make Halden protect the bond and cargo schedule without erasing the damaged tender crew or inventing evidence he does not possess.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: Embodied route expertise can support an inference, but it cannot make a missing interface channel retroactively present.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Let Sere reconstruct a bounded interval only when the record labels it as inference and preserves the channel failure.

observer_read: A poor station turning maintenance debt into claimant delay
A hearing clerk protecting procedure before cargo
target_self_read: A local court preserving a record that another corridor node can trust
Staff refusing to call partial access complete
misread_patterns: May treat a pause as obstruction because the schedule cost is immediate
May treat manual translation as repetition rather than new access
likely_insults: expensive redundancy with one working channel
factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Halden may resent the process without being written as hostile to uplift personhood or indifferent to rescue.

observer_read: A claimant trying to convert reputation and urgency into evidentiary weight
A carrier whose real rescue may still have an inaccurate account
target_self_read: A dependable crew being punished for spending time and propellant on another vessel
A carrier trying to keep necessary cargo moving
misread_patterns: Staff may mistake compressed operational speech for dishonesty
A correct insistence on provenance may underweight cargo and dependent costs
factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Keep Sere's skepticism bounded to the record; he must not infer selfish motive from Halden's urgency alone.

role_pressure_fields.summary: An uplifted cetacean clerk with local pause and disposition authority whose own access to the decisive record depends on station equipment.
obligations: Keep the hearing legible across bodies
Allocate or withhold the berth locally
failure_modes: Admitting a record he could not access
Rejecting thin evidence while exporting all cost to others
Using expertise to hide a failed channel
Requesting accommodation after allocation authority has already bitten

role_pressure_fields.summary: A baseline staffer who owns console operation, evidence transfer, manual translation, and the exact wording that will travel with the local decision.
obligations: Translate without upgrading testimony into sensor fact
Expose the clock and request owner
available_masks: Deliberate refusal to mirror claimant panic
failure_modes: Becoming the invisible human authority behind Sere's nominal decision
Letting translation labor disappear from the record
Treating a diagnostic receipt as restored access

role_pressure_fields.summary: A Lightsail captain who needs a rescue diversion admitted before a berth window and bond review close.
obligations: Account for formation break and propellant spend
Keep claimant testimony distinguishable from the sealed trace
available_masks: Direct appeal to the saved tender crew
failure_modes: Treating access work as station delay
Selecting timestamps that help the bond
Winning a berth through a record the clerk could not inspect

role_pressure_fields.summary: A junior dryside participant who can learn the trace through the tactile rail and become a witness to either shared practice or procedural exclusion.
obligations: Carry the practical lesson into later watches
available_masks: Brief delight when the cross-body pattern clicks
failure_modes: Confusing mirrored numbers with independent evidence
Learning that access is optional whenever a schedule is tight

known_context.text: Sere knows Brineglass's board, pool, paddle, evidence drawer, local clock rule, his own sensory limits, and the public stakes of this berth claim.

beliefs.text: Sere believes a decision must preserve which parts came from sensors, translation, claimant testimony, and embodied inference.

misreads.text: Sere may read Halden's compressed insurer language as stronger evidence of self-protection than it is.

must_not_know.text: Sere must not know whether Halden selected false timestamps or what later bond reviewers will decide.

known_context.text: Mina knows dryside console state, custody marks, clock behavior, claimant submissions, and the manual translation workflow she performs.

beliefs.text: Mina treats exact labels and visible costs as the tools available to a poor station.

misreads.text: Mina may underread Halden's cargo pressure because the console presents it as one more impatient claim.

must_not_know.text: Mina must not silently decide the berth while presenting Sere as the owner of the ruling.

known_context.text: Halden knows his ship's maneuver, cargo, propellant spend, duplicate timestamps, bond exposure, and the shrinking berth margin.

beliefs.text: Halden believes saving the tender and arriving with the cargo should make the hazard diversion operationally legible.

misreads.text: Halden may interpret the clock pause as Sere protecting procedure at the carrier's expense rather than protecting the evidence boundary.

must_not_know.text: Halden must not know how Sere experiences the missing pressure interval except through Sere's words and actions.

known_context.text: Toma knows the duplicate trace, the working raised notation, and any cross-channel pattern Sere explicitly teaches before the failure.

beliefs.text: Toma begins by treating careful custody as holding the slate correctly and may learn that provenance includes who could access the replay.

misreads.text: Toma may mistake a claimant timestamp matching the rail for independent confirmation.

must_not_know.text: Toma must not infer the missing pressure channel or Sere's private confidence without a visible label or statement.

author_only_boundaries.text: Brineglass is canonically a small outer-corridor stop with the fixture-marked room geometry, but its exact orbit, population, and later history remain unspecified.
Sere, Mina, Halden, Toma, Dawn Ledger, the damaged tender, and this hearing outcome are fixture-local draft elements, not promoted historical canon.
The fixture may use a bottlenose Navigator in 2671 because the same-era continuity contains one, but it must not import Choir-Speaker Nacre-in-Current or the pirate novella's events into Brineglass.

open_questions.question: Where exactly is Brineglass Waystation in the outer-corridor network?
open_questions.notes: The owning lore note intentionally calls it a small outer-corridor stop. The fixture does not assign an orbit or route endpoint.

open_questions.question: Which cetacean lineages and personal naming traditions are common at Brineglass?
open_questions.notes: The fixture uses one story-local bottlenose character and does not generalize the name Sere-in-Return into a coalition-wide convention.

open_questions.question: How are berth minutes, convoy bonds, and local delay costs represented in the future Aetheria economy schema?
open_questions.notes: The fixture keeps them as coarse local variables and material consequences rather than inventing a currency or universal tariff.
